bills.title: Data Centers (CS/CS/SB 484)
bills.statusNote: The Senate first passed the bill unanimously on Feb. 26, 2026; the House amended and passed it 92-16, the Senate concurred 31-6 on March 13, 2026, and Gov. DeSantis signed it May 7, 2026 as Chapter 2026-65, effective July 1, 2026.
bills.summary: Regulates large-scale data centers and other large-load electricity customers (50 MW or more), barring utilities from shifting the costs of serving them onto other customers, preserving local governments' authority to reject such facilities, and letting water regulators require alternative water sources. It also directs OPPAGA to study data center construction and operation and report by July 1, 2027.

bills.title: Public Records/Data Centers (CS/SB 1118)
bills.statusNote: The committee substitute from Community Affairs died on the Senate calendar when the regular session ended March 13, 2026; the House tracker cross-references the enacted SB 484.
bills.summary: Would have created a temporary public records exemption for information about a person's plans or interest in locating a data center in a county or municipality, tied to the effective date of SB 484 and subject to future legislative review and repeal.

bills.title: 2025 tax package (data center sales tax exemption changes)
bills.statusNote: Gov. DeSantis signed the $1.6 billion tax package on June 30, 2025; the data center change took effect Aug. 1, 2025.
bills.summary: Among other tax changes, limited the state sales tax exemption for data centers to facilities with at least 100 MW of critical IT load, with no grandfathering for smaller existing centers, and extended the deadline for exemption certificates from June 30, 2027 to June 30, 2037.

bills.title: Artificial Intelligence Bill of Rights (CS/SB 482)
bills.statusNote: The Senate passed it 35-2 on March 4, 2026, but the House never heard it and it died in messages on March 13, 2026; House companion HB 1395 died in the Information Technology Budget & Policy Subcommittee the same day.
bills.summary: Would have created a state 'Artificial Intelligence Bill of Rights,' including rules barring companion chatbots from interacting with minors without parental consent and requiring chatbots to disclose that they are not human. It was the legislative vehicle for Gov. DeSantis's AI proposal; House Speaker Daniel Perez said AI should be handled at the federal level.

bills.statusNote: Announced at a news conference in The Villages on Dec. 4, 2025; the proposals were later carried by SB 482 (AI) and SB 484 (data centers).

bills.statusNote: Speaking Dec. 15, 2025, days after President Trump's Dec. 11, 2025 order on a national AI policy framework, DeSantis said Florida would proceed with its AI Bill of Rights.

bills.title: Removal of Altered Sexual Depictions Posted Without Consent ("Brooke's Law")
bills.statusNote: Passed the House April 16 and the Senate April 23, 2025; signed by Gov. DeSantis in Jacksonville on June 10, 2025 as Chapter 2025-133.
bills.summary: Requires platforms that host user-generated content to set up a process, by Dec. 31, 2025, for people to request removal of nonconsensual altered sexual depictions (deepfakes) of themselves and to remove them within 48 hours of a valid request, with platforms facing lawsuits for noncompliance.

bills.statusNote: The House passed it unanimously (reported as March 5, 2026), but it died in the Senate when the session ended March 13, 2026; Senate companion SB 202 also died.
bills.summary: Would have required a qualified human professional to make insurance claim denial or reduction decisions, barred AI output from being the sole basis for a denial, and required insurers to document AI use in claims-handling manuals.
